naslov: Be a Fragrance Everyone Senses but No One Sees

segmenti.tekst: إِنَّ الْحَمْدَ لِلَّهِ نَحْمَدُهُ وَنَسْتَعِينُهُ وَنَسْتَغْفِرُهُ
segmenti.prevod: Indeed, all praise belongs to Allah; we praise Him, seek His help and ask His forgiveness.

segmenti.tekst: وَنَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنْ شُرُورِ أَنْفُسِنَا وَمِنْ سَيِّئَاتِ أَعْمَالِنَا مَنْ يَهْدِهِ اللَّهُ فَلَا مُضِلَّ لَهُ، وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُ
segmenti.prevod: We seek refuge in Allah from the evils of our souls and from our bad deeds. Whomever Allah guides, none can lead astray, and whomever He leaves astray, none can guide.

segmenti.tekst: وَأَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَرْسَلَهُ اللَّهُ بِالْحَقِّ بَشِيرًا وَنَذِيرًا وَسِرَاجًا مُنِيرًا لِيُنْذِرَ مَنْ كَانَ حَيًّا وَيَحِقَّ الْقَوْلُ عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ صَلَّى اللَّهُ تَعَالَى عَلَيْهِ وَعَلَى آلِهِ الطَّيِّبِينَ الطَّاهِرِينَ وَأَصْحَابِهِ الْكِرَامِ الْهُدَاةِ الْمُهْتَدِينَ وَسَلَّمَ تَسْلِيمًا كَثِيرًا إِلَى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ
segmenti.prevod: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, Who has no partner, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and messenger. Allah sent him with the truth as a bearer of glad tidings, a warner and a light-giving lamp, to warn whoever is alive (of heart) and so that the Word may be fulfilled against the disbelievers (Ya-Sin 36:70). May Allah the Exalted bless him and his good and pure family and his noble companions, the rightly guided who guided others, and grant him abundant peace until the Day of Judgement.

segmenti.tekst: قَالَ اللَّهُ فِي كِتَابِهِ الْكَرِيمِ يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ تُقَاتِهِ وَلَا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ أَمَّا بَعْدُ
segmenti.prevod: Allah says in His noble Book: “O you who believe, fear Allah as He deserves to be feared, and do not die except as Muslims.” (Al Imran 3:102). To proceed:

segmenti.tekst: Praise belongs to Allah alone, the Exalted, subhanahu wa ta'ala, the Lord of all the worlds, the Lord of the Day of Judgement, the Lord of jinn and mankind. May blessings and peace be upon His Messenger, the beloved Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), upon his family, upon his companions, and upon all those who follow the path, the path of the Qur'an, the path of the Sunnah of Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam.
Respected brothers, when Musa reached Madyan, utterly exhausted and afraid, fleeing from Pharaoh and his men, he took shelter in a shade near a spring.
And at that spring there were many shepherds trying to water their flocks.

And so Musa, alayhis-salatu was-salam, while resting from that hard journey which had drained him both physically and mentally, noticed two young women trying to water their flocks, two weak young women.

So Musa, alayhis-salatu was-salam, tired and exhausted as he was, approached them and asked them: "What are you doing? Do you need anything?" They said: "We cannot water our flocks until these shepherds disperse, until they have finished."
So Musa, alayhis-salatu was-salam, exhausted as he was, took their flocks and watered them. And then he went back to the place in the shade where he had been resting.
You see, dear brothers, this story that the Qur'an tells us is not just some mere story for a person to hear. Rather, when the Qur'an tells us something, it wants us to take a lesson from it.

Every Qur'anic story, every Qur'anic ayah, is a lesson for the believer. And the lesson of this, of this story, is that a Muslim, a believer, however tired he may be, however many trials and problems of his own he may have, must not forget his Muslim brother.
He must not forget his Muslim brother. So we see: Musa, alayhis-salam, in such a state, did not forget to help others.

A believer, a mu'min, ought to have a little psychology in him. And all of us, wallahi, do have it, even though we may never have studied psychology. That is, when we see on our brother's face that he has some problem, some distress,

we should ask him: "Brother, do you need anything?" – just as Musa, alayhis-salatu was-salam, did. "Can we help you somehow? In what way can we help you?" And all of us, all of us notice this in our Muslim brother.

All of us. Whenever someone is in distress, in a difficult state, all of us notice it. Believe me, dear brothers, to us it may be something small, that question may not mean much to us, but to the one who is in some distress or trial, believe me, it means a great deal.
Believe me, it means a great deal. What should a believer, a mu'min, be like? He should be like a fragrance: sensed, but not seen.
We have the example of a great scholar, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, who, it is said, every morning would bring food to the doorsteps of the poor and leave it there.

Those poor people would sense that fragrance, but they did not know, they never saw Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak bringing them that food. Only when he passed away did they see how much he had meant to them.

They realised that it was, that Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak was that fragrance which they sensed but did not see. That is what a believer should be like. A believer should constantly keep in mind the words of Allah: "Man 'amila salihan min dhakarin aw untha" – "Whoever does a righteous deed, whether male or female," He says, "We will surely grant them a good life." You see, dear brothers, how Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala,

does not promise a reward only in that world… not only in the Hereafter, but also in this one, in this world as well. He promises a reward to whoever does a good deed, to whoever helps his Muslim brother; He promises him a reward in this world. He says: "We will grant him…" – whether he has lived, whether he has lived through this life – Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, will never humiliate the believer, the one who helped others, never. And He says: "And We will reward them

in the Hereafter according to the best of what they used to do" in this world. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, promises a reward for a good deed in this world, and that is a good life, and in the next, in the next the reward, dear brothers, is great, and that is Jannah (Paradise). Also, whoever does even an atom's weight of good will see it; Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ" – whoever does even an atom's weight of good will see it.

And of course, whoever does even an atom's weight of evil will see it. I ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to make us among His sincere servants. I ask Him, the Exalted, to help us be good, true believers, to help us be among those who help one another and come to one another's aid.
I ask Him, the Exalted, to protect us from every evil, to forgive our sins and the sins of our parents, and to admit us into Jannah. Amin, ya Rabbal-'alamin.
أَقُولُ قَوْلِي هَٰذَا وَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ لِي وَلَكُمْ فَاسْتَغْفِرُوهُ إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ
segmenti.prevod: I say these words of mine and ask Allah for forgiveness for myself and for you, so ask Him for forgiveness; truly He is the Oft-Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
